messages:
alex: Heads-up — onboarding run for harpoon-compact-int4 on staging shows recall@1 down ~7% vs fp16 baseline on multilingual holdout. Starting a thread to triage.

morgan: Which holdout? Short queries or long?

alex: It's the mixed holdout: short (<=4 tokens) + long (8-16 tokens). The drop is concentrated in the long tail (8-12 tokens).

jia: Can you paste the quick stats?

alex: ```
model: harpoon-compact-int4
baseline fp16 recall@1: 0.78
int4 recall@1: 0.71
recall@5: 0.92 -> 0.89
mean cosine baseline: 0.42
mean cosine int4 : 0.37
centroid drift (L2) ~ 0.06
```

pat: Oof. Mean cosine shift + centroid drift suggests quantization noise isn't symmetric. Did we use per-channel quantization?

alex: Yes, per-channel. We used the usual calibration set (200k samples).

morgan: Any preprocessing differences between offline eval and embedding-serving? Normalization/whitening?

alex: Good call — offline eval pipeline runs unicode nfkc, aggressive token normalization, and then L2 renorm; the serving binary had a lightweight normalizer (NFKC not applied) and a different renorm order (whitening then renorm).

jia: That explains it. Whitening+quantization can amplify small preprocessing shifts.

eval-bot: New eval artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/inference/artifacts/3462109876/harpoon-int4-evals — contains per-query diffs, embedding histograms, and cluster plots.

pat: Looking at the artifact: cluster plots show one anchor cluster splitting into two along a single principal axis after quant. Long-tail queries map to the lower branch.

morgan: Quick experiments to try: 1) force identical preprocessing (NFKC + same tokenizer) 2) move renorm before whitening 3) try clamp range [-6,6] during quant calibration 4) test per-channel asymmetric scale vs symmetric.

alex: Started 1 and 3 locally. Early result: forcing NFKC + exact tokenizer recovers ~3% of the drop. Clamp helped another ~1.5%. Still ~2.5% missing.

jia: Can you paste the eval command you ran?

alex: ```bash
PYTHONPATH=./tests ./scripts/run_eval.py \
  --model harpoon-compact-int4 \
  --holdout multilingual-mix.json \
  --preproc nfkc --tokenizer v3 --renorm after_whiten \
  --calib-clamp 6 --perchannel true \
  --out /tmp/eval_harpoon_int4.json
```

pat: Try renorm before whitening (we've seen that reduce directionality shifts). Also run a small subset with fp16 but apply the int4 quantization noise model (simulate quant noise) to confirm it's quant noise vs model topology.

morgan: Also check pooling: harpoon uses mean pooling on last 4 tokens by default? If long queries include trailing context, pooling differences can amplify.

alex: Harpoon default is mean over token embeddings (all tokens). I will try CLS pooling + mean-of-last-4 as ablation.

jia: Another diagnostic: compute per-query delta = cosine(fp16, int4) and sort by delta. If top deltas correspond to certain language families or punctuation patterns, could be tokenization edgecases.

eval-bot: Quick stat from artifact: top 500 delta queries are enriched for Spanish/Portuguese and for queries with 2+ punctuation marks.

pat: That smells like tokenizer mismatch + rare subword rounding. Good catch.

alex: Plan: (A) enforce identical preprocessing across offline/serving, (B) run renorm-before-whiten experiment, (C) try asymmetric per-channel quant scales, (D) run pooling ablations. I'll post new artifacts.

morgan: Thanks — if A recovers most, we should add a preflight check in onboarding: assert mean/var of a 10k sample between offline and serving match within eps.

jia: +1 on preflight check. Also add per-language spot-checks for centroids.

alex: Will follow up in this thread. tagging @pat for quant tuning help. :mag:

pat: I can help this afternoon. If we still see residual drop after A/C, we'll try small increase in calibration set and test per-channel zero-point adjustments.

alex: Great. Last note: no customer-facing impact yet (staging only) but good to close the loop before production.

morgan: Nice triage so far. Keep it short updates here. :thumbsup:
